Trade-finance workflow

After this lesson you can:
  • Handle instruments, documents and sanctions in cross-border trade
  • Understand contingent versus funded exposure

Learning rhythm: read one section at a time, pause to explain the control in your own words, then answer the knowledge check without looking back.

1. The product

The documentary end of trade: letters of credit, guarantees and collections, where the bank's promise (a contingent exposure) substitutes for trust between distant counterparties, becoming funded only if drawn. The workflow examines documents, not goods: instrument terms, shipment documents, customs evidence — discrepancies between them are the daily work.

Cross-border means sanctions screening on every party and route, currency in minor units of its own denomination, incoterms allocating who bears what, and SWIFT messaging as the transport.

2. What a BA watches

Trade-based money laundering is the AML frontier — over/under-invoicing and phantom shipments launder value through exactly these instruments, which is why screening and document examination are contract facts. Contingent accounting (exposure without disbursement) is unlike every other journey; treat it as its own discipline.

Knowledge check

Answer aloud or write your choice before opening the explanation. If you miss it, revisit the named section—not the whole lesson.

1. Banks in documentary trade deal in…

  1. Goods
  2. Documents — conformity of papers to instrument terms, not the cargo itself
  3. Ships
  4. Warehouses
Reveal answer and reasoning

B. The instrument obliges payment against conforming documents; examination and discrepancy management are the craft.
